transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-22
Start: 16:00 UTC, Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, TidePoint), Marcus Yao (Platform), Priya Nair (CTO), Aaron Cole (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Customer is building a docs + chat assistant; main concerns are p95 latency under load and steady tokens/sec during streaming. Evaluating Redwood Hosted for speed vs Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private for compliance.

[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, i'm Maya with Redwood, and with me is Ravi our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Priya: good, thanks. we'll kick off — we've been wanting to talk p95 and throughput, so excited to get into it.
[00:00:20] Lena: yes hi, lena here. short context: TidePoint is building an assistant on top of our internal docs and a summarization pipeline. expecting a mix of short Q&A and long form summarization — some responses up to 800-1,200 tokens.
[00:00:33] Marcus: and from platform side we care about concurrency — initial user base 200-500 concurrent, can spike to 3k in marketing blasts.
[00:00:42] Maya: perfect, that's exactly the detail we need. Ravi i'll hand to you for a quick overview of options (hosted/dedicated/private) and how they change p95 and tokens/sec.
[00:00:51] Ravi: thanks maya. quick note — i'll probably mangle some product names, so forgive me if i say Redwood Dedi- or Redwood Privet, um. high level: Hosted has fastest time to market and the best ops lift; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and is our sweet spot for steady p95 SLAs; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance and data residency, you get full control but setup time and ops are higher.
[00:01:15] Ravi: on latency: for short queries (~32-128 tokens) we often see p95 in the 60-140ms range on Hosted depending on model; Dedicated can tighten that to sub-100ms p95 for optimized models. For streaming long outputs, it's less about single p95 and more about token/sec sustained rate and the p95 of chunk latencies — customers often target p95 chunk latency < 200ms and average tokens/sec of 35-120 depending on model/quantization.
[00:01:45] Aaron: when you say chunk latency, is that per token or per 256-token chunk? we do chunking at 512 tokens.
[00:01:52] Ravi: good question — our runtime emits streaming chunks often every 64-256 tokens depending on the tokenizer and model; if you're chunking at 512 you'll see larger intervals, so p95 can inflate. we can tune to emit smaller chunks but there's tradeoff with per-chunk overhead.
[00:02:10] Lena: our p95 target for short replies is 120ms — anything above that feels laggy. for long summaries we want the tail to be sub-800ms for the first 200 tokens and then steady tokens/sec. is that realistic?
[00:02:23] Ravi: yes those are reasonable; short replies at p95 120ms is achievable on Dedicated for many open models, with proper batching and cache priming. for the long summaries you'll want to look at sustained token/sec and prefix cache. do you have sample prompts we can use to benchmark?
[00:02:36] Lena: we can share 10-15 canonical prompts, mixed short/long. we'll attach them after the call.

[00:03:02] Speaker 1: (mumble) can you talk about concurrency and steady-state? i.e., how many tokens/sec per GPU in practice?
[00:03:08] Ravi: rough numbers — for a 7B float16 open model on an A100-equivalent, steady-state token/sec per GPU might be 300-800 tokens/sec depending on sequence length distribution and batching. for quantized 4-bit models that improves. higher model sizes drop tokens/sec substantially. but real world numbers vary a lot based on prompt lengths and streaming config.
[00:03:30] Marcus: what about scaling — do you autoscale dedicated pools? and what's the burst look like?
[00:03:36] Maya: yes we have configurable autoscaling for Dedicated with burst capacity; you can set thresholds by latency or queue depth and we also support automatic fallback to hosted models if capacity is constrained.
[00:03:49] Marcus: fallback to hosted — so data path crosses public API? that's a security concern.
[00:03:54] Maya: it can, we support policies to restrict failover and also a private fallback within your VPC for Private deployments. for Hosted+Dedic customers, fallbacks are opt-in and can be configured to not send PII.
[00:04:08] Priya: can you walk through an example benchmark plan? we want apples-to-apples with our current OpenAI setup.
[00:04:15] Ravi: sure — plan: provide 10 canonical prompts, instrument a synthetic traffic shape (200 steady, short bursts to 3k), run with streaming enabled and disabled, collect p50/p95/p99 latencies for initial token and per-chunk, and measure sustained tokens/sec for 5-10 minute windows. we can mirror your OpenAI config — same model family, same temperature, same chunking.
[00:04:36] Lena: do you support token-level tracing so we can map where latency comes from? network vs compile vs kernel?
[00:04:42] Ravi: yes our Console gives per-request traces and token-level timing when you enable debug traces; note that debug tracing adds overhead so for production benchmarks we do sampling.

[00:05:12] Marcus: on the security checklist — SOC2, SSO support, KMS integration for Private, audit logs, data retention controls — do you have those?
[00:05:20] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II; support SAML/SSO and SCIM; Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. for hosted we have encryption at rest and customer key options for some tiers.
[00:05:33] Priya: ok good. one concern: our legal team will ask about egress control and log retention for Hosted.
[00:05:38] Maya: absolutely — i'll include our security pack with explicit answers and retention policies.

[00:06:05] Lena: cost is important — can you ballpark cost difference between hosted and dedicated for our expected load (200 steady, 3k occasional spike)? we currently pay per-token with OpenAI and want predictable monthly.
[00:06:16] Maya: roughly speaking, Hosted is per-token and good for smaller or variable usage; Dedicated is larger commit but often lower unit cost and predictable. we can produce a cost model once you share token distribution and prompts; i'll send a pricing spreadsheet.
[00:06:29] Priya: what's the onboarding time for Private? we might need VPC option for compliance.
[00:06:35] Ravi: Private onboarding is typically 4-8 weeks depending on infra and whether you're on-prem vs VPC. includes install, KMS integration, and any network peering. Dedicated is usually faster — days to weeks.

[00:07:02] Marcus: for benchmarks, do you require a full model checkpoint or will a distilled sample suffice?
[00:07:07] Ravi: we prefer a representative model or close variant; if you can't share, we can use a similar open model + your prompt set. but for quantization and kernel tuning it's ideal to have the actual weights or a reproducible config.
[00:07:22] Aaron: can we test quantized profiles? we run 4-bit quantization in prod.
[00:07:26] Ravi: yes, we support quantization-aware kernels and can benchmark 4-bit/8-bit profiles. note that quality regressions are possible and we have tooling to run evals against your prompt set to detect regressions.

[00:07:48] Lena: i want to call out a strict p95 SLA requirement for our legal team: 120ms p95 for short chat responses under normal load. can Redwood commit to that on Dedicated?
[00:07:58] Maya: we can commit SLA targets for Dedicated with appropriate sizing and a reserve. exact SLA wording will go into the contract; our performance team will size the pool for your p95 with buffer.
[00:08:09] Priya: is there an escape hatch at busy times? we need graceful degradation not 500s.
[00:08:14] Ravi: we provide graceful degradation via fallbacks (lighter model, cached prefixes) and queueing with early abort. also Circuit-breaker policies to prevent cascading failures.

[00:09:00] Speaker 2: can you share example numbers for tokens/sec per GPU at different models?
[00:09:06] Ravi: example heuristics: 7B f16 ~ 400-800 tokens/sec per A100-GPU; 13B f16 ~ 150-300; 70B f16 ~ 30-90. with 4-bit quant we might get 1.5-2x improvement but depends on kernels. Those are ballpark.
[00:09:24] Marcus: ok, for our mix we'd probably land in 13B-ish or quantized 70B to keep quality, so we need a conservative model for capacity planning.

[00:09:46] Maya: quick operational question — how do you handle KV cache for multi-turn chat?
[00:09:51] Ravi: we keep per-session KV cache; cache size impacts memory and latency. for Dedicated we can guarantee enough KV cache capacity per session; for Hosted we provide best-effort and recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts.

[00:10:20] Priya: what's the instrumentation overhead for tracing? i.e., will tracing change the benchmark numbers?
[00:10:26] Ravi: sampled tracing has minimal overhead; full token-level tracing can add 5-20% latency depending on the hooks. we recommend sampling during load tests and full traces in smaller runs.

[00:11:00] Lena: okay let's talk failure modes — what happens when a GPU saturates? are requests queued? dropped?
[00:11:07] Ravi: requests are queued in the runtime with backpressure; we can configure timeouts and early responses for degraded modes. when saturation hits autoscaling thresholds we'll spin up more Dedicated nodes or route to fallback. there's also a configurable reject policy to fail fast for certain classes of requests.

[00:12:30] Maya: do you have any strict data residency requirements (country-level) or can we host everything in a single region?
[00:12:36] Priya: for now US east is fine but some customers require EU data residency for EU users. we may need multi-region later.
[00:12:43] Maya: Redwood supports region pinning for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has regional endpoints for EU/US as well.

[00:13:10] Marcus: for the pilot, we'd like to measure p95 under a synthetic traffic pattern: steady 200, bursts to 3k for 3 minutes every hour, and a long-run sustained token generation test for 30 minutes. can Redwood run that?
[00:13:21] Ravi: yes we can. we'll instrument and provide p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec time series.

[00:14:02] Speaker 3: any concerns with network egress on Private?
[00:14:06] Marcus: egress bandwidth for streamed tokens — do you shard across pods or keep single stream per session?
[00:14:11] Ravi: streaming uses persistent connection to a single serving node while the session is warm; we can proxy across nodes but that adds latency. for Private we typically peer directly.

[00:15:00] Priya: one more on SLAs: do you include p95 measurements in the monthly SLA report?
[00:15:06] Maya: yes Dedicated customers get monthly performance reports with p50/p95/p99 and token costs by model/route.

[00:16:18] Lena: let's talk about the benchmark deliverables — what format will you return results in? csv, dashboards?
[00:16:24] Ravi: we'll provide a dashboard link from Redwood Console plus raw CSVs with per-request timing and token/sec time series. we'll also include a short findings doc with recommended configuration (batching, kv-cache, quantization profile).

[00:18:40] Aaron: what about cold start behavior for streaming sessions?
[00:18:44] Ravi: cold start can add 30-300ms depending on model and whether weights are warmed; Dedicated with pinned models lowers cold start variance. we can pre-warm frequently used models.

[00:20:01] Marcus: do you integrate with our observability stack? like Prometheus and Sentry?
[00:20:05] Ravi: yes we can export Prometheus metrics and traces; we also have webhook alerts and support for Datadog.

[00:22:12] Priya: any gotchas with function calling or tool invocation and streaming? we do tool-call heavy flows.
[00:22:19] Ravi: function/tool calls are supported; streaming plus tool calls means you sometimes have to buffer until tool outputs; we provide structured output helpers to make that reliable. there can be added latency around the external call.

[00:24:00] Maya: thanks — quick commercial note: for Dedicated we usually size a reserve that covers steady load and commit week — that impacts price. we'll model that once we get the prompts.

[00:26:30] Lena: are there any public perf numbers you can share vs OpenAI for our use case?
[00:26:36] Maya: we have internal benchmarks and a model catalog with throughput profiles; we'll share a anonymized benchmark showing p95 and tokens/sec for various models to help you calibrate against OpenAI numbers.

[00:28:12] Marcus: i'm curious about preemptible vs preemptible GPUs — do you use spot instances in Dedicated?
[00:28:18] Ravi: Dedicated pools are usually on reserved/ondemand, not preemptible, because of the p95 SLOs. for non-critical workloads we can use spot to lower cost with fallback.

[00:30:00] Maya: jumping ahead to plan — we'll do a two-stage pilot: 1) bench & tune (1 week) with your prompts; 2) small canary in prod with 200 steady users for 2 weeks. if that looks good we expand.
[00:30:15] Priya: timeline-wise that fits. any blockers from Redwood side?
[00:30:21] Maya: just prompts and a decision on whether you want Hosted test or Dedicated pilot. we'll also need a contact for security questions.

[00:32:10] Lena: i'll own prompts, Priya will handle stakeholder approval, Marcus will coordinate infra.
[00:32:18] Marcus: yep

[00:33:00] Speaker 1 (muttering): what about A/B testing and rollouts?
[00:33:05] Ravi: Redwood has rollout mechanics — canary, A/B, auto-fallback based on error rates and latency. we'll include that in the pilot plan.

[00:35:40] Priya: any reference customers with similar scale?
[00:35:45] Maya: we can share anonymized references; i'll include a short case study about a customer with 1k steady and burst to 5k.

[00:37:20] Aaron: last technical Q — do you support streaming with HTTP/2 or do you require websocket?
[00:37:26] Ravi: we support both HTTP/2 chunked streaming and websocket streaming; choice depends on client.

[00:39:10] Lena: ok let's recap next steps.
[00:39:14] Maya: recap: 1) tidepoint supplies prompts and sample dataset by 2027-03-25; 2) ravi runs bench and returns CSV + dashboard by 2027-03-29; 3) maya sends pricing and security pack by 2027-03-24; 4) schedule pilot for week of 2027-04-11.
[00:39:36] Priya: agreed.
[00:39:40] Marcus: one more — can we get an initial capacity estimate sooner, just rough numbers to budget?
[00:39:45] Ravi: yes we'll provide a capacity estimate with conservative buffers in the benchmark deliverable.

[00:41:00] Maya: cool thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs. any final quick questions?
[00:41:07] Lena: none, thanks.
[00:41:10] Priya: thanks all.
[00:41:14] Maya: bye

(End of call)
